newsitem.title: JAPAN: Famine-stricken North Korea exports corn to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Famine-stricken North Korea exports corn to Japan.

text.p: Famine-stricken North Korea has just exported more than 1,000 tonnes of corn to Japan and the grain was being unloaded on Thursday at a northern Japan port, customs officials said.

A spokesman for the Aomori Customs Office said the 3,317-tonne passenger-freighter Mangyongbong '92, the only North Korean ship that regularly sails to Japan, was expected to finish unloading 1,030 tonnes of maize at Aomori port, 600 km (375 miles) north of Tokyo, later on Thursday.
The spokesman said the cargo was loaded at the North Korean port of Chongjin on July 12, but refused to reveal the buyer.
"The North Korean ship is unloading the corn but we have not made public the buyer of the cargo," the spokesman told Reuters.
Japanese government spokesman Kaoru Yosano said the government was investigating the case.
"This is a transaction between private firms but we are investigating the case," Yosano, the deputy chief cabinet secretary, told a news conference.
The Japanese newspaper Sankei Shimbun said a poultry farmer in Yokohama, which adjoins Tokyo, ordered the grain as chicken feed through an unnamed Japan-based North Korean trading company.
The newspaper estimated the cargo was worth 13 million yen ($112,000).
The daily said it was the first such export of unprocessed livestock feed from North Korea since 1988.

The customs spokesman said the corn was in "bulk form" and did not come in bags or other containers which could show its origin, particularly if the maize might be connected to international aid relief.
Japanese officials said they were surprised at how North Korea was able to export grain when it was receiving food aid from international organisations and various countries.
Food aid, such as from North Korea's bitter rival South Korea, includes corn as well as rice.
The U.N World Food Programme has said North Korea, hit by two years of devastating floods which washed away rice paddies, needs more than 1.2 million tonnes of food this year to feed its population.
Members of international aid missions to North Korea have reported that many of the communist nation's residents are badly malnourished from the severe food shortages.
They have said that in some areas people were eating grass and tree bark to supplement their meagre diet. ($1=116 yen)
